narrative.overview: The site is built the way the devices are made: in layers, to measure. A white build plate carries full-width navy strata, each striped with fine horizontal layer lines, like a part seen from the side while it prints. Lime is the layer printing right now: it marks the one thing to read or do in each region, and never more than that.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, navy strata with layer lines, lime as the single "active" accent.
Montserrat 800 for headings set in stacked lines; Atkinson Hyperlegible for every sentence.
3px rules and 2px corners; no cards with drop shadows.
The signature: a device that builds itself layer by layer on load, and a step ruler that fills as you scroll.

rules.name: The Navy-On-Lime Rule
rules.body: Text on lime is navy (or black in high contrast). White on lime is 1.29:1 and is never used.

rules.name: The One Active Layer Rule
rules.body: Lime marks one thing per region: the action or the phrase that matters.

rules.name: The Bordered Lime Rule
rules.body: Every lime control on a light ground carries a 3px navy border to stay visible as a component.

rules.name: The Fits-At-150 Rule
rules.body: Large titles use min(size, Ncqi) so they fit at 320px with text at 150%.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small label above a heading. Numbers appear only where sequence matters.

rules.name: The Strata Rule
rules.body: Separate regions with a change of band, not with shadows or boxes.

dos: Do put navy text on lime, always (13.7:1).
Do give every lime control on white a 3px navy border.
Do build sizes in rem and breakpoints in container queries, so the text-size control reflows the page.
Do keep every touch target at 44×44px or more.
Do use layer lines on navy bands and placeholders as the brand texture.
donts: Don't use white text on lime (1.29:1).
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't use drop shadows to separate content; change the band.
Don't use lime for more than one element per region.
Don't show hover effects without the (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) gate.
